persona.name: Independent restaurant owner
persona.tagline: Owner-operator of a small trattoria or café who runs the book and pays for the tool
persona.description: Runs a 22–52 seat place with a partner and handles bookings personally, from phone, widget, Instagram DMs and WhatsApp. Lucia (Casa Verde) pays $79/month for BookBistro plus ~$40 in SMS overage and loses 25–30 minutes a day fixing the book; Tomasz (Kettle & Crumb) runs a WhatsApp-plus-paper-book flow he mostly considers fine. Both want boring reliability and no setup burden, but they split sharply on price ($89–90 all-in vs. $15–20), SMS and deposits.
goals: Keep one reliable book with no double-bookings or overfilled nights
Keep no-shows low without hurting the friendly mood of the place
Pay one predictable price that matches the size of the business
Switch tools only in a quiet month and without retyping guest history
frustrations: Re-typing Instagram and WhatsApp bookings by hand every evening
Reminders that silently stop and support that takes three days
Metered SMS that turns a $79 plan into ~$120
Setup that demands floor plans, zones and turn times for a one-table café
persona.evidence_note: Two owners interviewed directly (Lucia, Tomasz), both with 'does'/'pays' evidence, plus second-hand remarks from a host (Oksana) and a floor manager (Devon) about their owners. The two owners run very different businesses (52-seat dinner trattoria vs. 22-seat café with a weekly supper), so most findings rest on one of them and disagree on SMS, deposits and price.

jobs.statement: When a booking arrives by phone, DM or WhatsApp, I want it in one book in one step, so I can stop re-typing and never double-book.
When a booking's day comes, I want reminders to go out reliably, so I can keep no-shows near 9% instead of 15%.
When a large party books a prime night, I want a small deposit, so I can protect the food and seats I've committed.
When service is running, I want to see real table status and realistic turn times, so I can seat the next party without sticky notes.
When a weeknight slot sits empty, I want to offer it to people waiting, so I can fill the 8:30 gap.
When I decide to switch tools, I want my guest history moved and a setup with no drawing or tutorial, so I can switch without retraining staff mid-season.
When I look at what the tool costs, I want one all-in price that fits my size, so I can weigh it against a lost Saturday.
When the Wi-Fi or the vendor fails, I want a fallback, so I can still run the night.

journey.title: Pick a booking tool
journey.goal: Choose a tool they trust without a long comparison or a big monthly fee

pains.text: SeatNow's $49/month felt like twelve sourdough loaves a week to Tomasz, so he cancelled the trial a day before it converted.
Tomasz is nervous about customers' phone numbers sitting in an unknown vendor's cloud after a booking-company leak.
At Harbor & Pine, switching needs an owner who doesn't like change.

jobs.text: Try a tool free for a month before committing, knowing the paper book may win.

tools.text: BookBistro Pro at $79/month (Casa Verde), a SeatNow trial at $49/month (Kettle & Crumb), SeatNow at ~$129/month (Harbor & Pine).

our_flow.text: No interviewee uses Tably; a free or very cheap tier is the only entry point Tomasz would try.

features.text: All-in pricing with a small-café tier

journey.title: Set up and migrate
journey.goal: Get running with their guest history and without retraining or drawing anything

pains.text: Two years of guest history, phone numbers and allergy notes sit in a BookBistro CSV with wrong columns.
SeatNow asked Tomasz to draw a floor plan and set turn times and zones for one long table.
Retraining 12 staff before the holidays is a no-go; January is the only window Lucia would consider.

jobs.text: Start without a tutorial or a twenty-option screen.

tools.text: BookBistro CSV export; a hardback paper book with a page per day.

our_flow.text: Tably has no tested import from BookBistro or a minimal one-table mode yet.

features.text: BookBistro import and no-drawing quick setup

journey.title: Take bookings from every channel
journey.goal: Get every request into one correct book quickly

pains.text: Phone and online bookings collide on one table once or twice a month because BookBistro's map doesn't refresh.
Lucia types about 15 Instagram and WhatsApp bookings into BookBistro every evening.
BookBistro's Google button shows 'no availability' when tables are free, losing bookings unnoticed.
Tomasz once wrote Friday on the Thursday page: 14 guests arrived, the book said 6.

jobs.text: Bring phone (~40%), widget (~35%), Instagram DMs and WhatsApp into one book.
Turn a WhatsApp message into a booking with one button.

tools.text: WhatsApp Business (~70% of Tomasz's supper bookings), paper book, BookBistro widget, Google listing and Instagram bio link.

our_flow.text: Gap: Tably doesn't capture DMs or WhatsApp; Tomasz says copying by hand only takes 10–15 minutes a day.

features.text: Conflict-locked shared book with a capacity warning

journey.title: Reduce no-shows
journey.goal: Make sure booked guests show up without souring the welcome

pains.text: When BookBistro's reminders stopped for 8 days, no-shows rose from ~9% to ~15%.
An 11-person Saturday no-show cost Casa Verde about $600.
Per-message SMS fees push Lucia to send fewer reminders.

jobs.text: Deposit only parties of six or more on Fridays and Saturdays, at $15 a head.
Remind supper guests personally on the day over WhatsApp and call non-repliers.

tools.text: BookBistro email and SMS reminders (300 texts included, 7¢ after); same-day WhatsApp messages by hand.

our_flow.text: Gap: owners disagree on paying for SMS at all; Tomasz relies on free WhatsApp and a ~3% no-show rate.

features.text: Included reminders over SMS or WhatsApp with send monitoring
Targeted refundable deposits for large parties and prime slots

journey.title: Seat and turn tables
journey.goal: Know which tables are free and when, without side notes

pains.text: BookBistro doesn't talk to Square, so the host tracks seated and paid tables on sticky notes.
Lucia spends 25–30 minutes a day fixing the book and her host another ~20 during service.
Fixed two-hour bookings ignore 90-minute Tuesdays and 2.5-hour Saturdays.

jobs.text: Keep running through Wi-Fi or power outages, which hit Kettle & Crumb twice last winter.
Get warned before booking more than 22 people on one evening.

tools.text: Sticky notes, Square POS, the paper book as an offline backup.

our_flow.text: Gap: no POS link or learned turn times; for a one-table café this screen may not matter at all.

features.text: Live table status with Square sync and learned turn times

journey.title: Fill empty slots
journey.goal: Turn cancellations and quiet weeknight slots into covers

pains.text: The 8:30 slot on Tuesdays and Wednesdays rarely fills.

jobs.text: Text waiting guests when a table opens.

tools.text: A paper waitlist on Saturdays that usually gets forgotten.

our_flow.text: Tably's waitlist could offer freed slots, but no owner has tested it; evidence is one owner's 'said'.

features.text: Waitlist that offers freed slots by text

journey.title: Review cost and reliability
journey.goal: Pay a fair, predictable price for something that doesn't break

pains.text: BookBistro's $79 plan becomes ~$120 with ~900 texts at 7¢ over the 300 included.
Support starts with a chatbot and a human ticket took three days.

jobs.text: Weigh the fee against a bad weekend's $300–400 loss, not the sticker price.

tools.text: BookBistro Pro $79 plus SMS overage; SeatNow ~$129/month at a 90-seat restaurant.

our_flow.text: Tably pricing is open: Lucia would pay $89–90 all-in, Tomasz $15–20 at most.

features.text: All-in pricing tiers with SMS included

opportunities.title: Never double-book or overfill a night
Keep reminders flowing without a per-message penalty
Know when a table will really be free
Fill weeknight gaps and late cancellations
Switch without losing history or retraining
Pay a price that fits the size of the place
Keep running when the internet or the vendor fails

solutions.title: Capture DM and WhatsApp bookings
solutions.description: Turn an Instagram DM or WhatsApp message into a booking in one tap, with the reply and confirmation sent back in the same thread. Removes the nightly re-typing and the wrong-page errors.
solutions.rationale: Two owners do this manually today (Lucia ~15 messages a night), but Tomasz says it only costs him 10–15 minutes, so impact is high rather than massive.

solutions.title: Lock the shared book against conflicts
solutions.description: One real-time book for phone, widget, Google and messages that blocks double-bookings, keeps Google availability in sync and warns before a night exceeds capacity.
solutions.rationale: Double-bookings and false 'no availability' cost real nights for both owners ('does' evidence), and reliability is the first thing Lucia asks for.

solutions.title: Include reminders in the plan
solutions.description: Day-before and day-of reminders over SMS or WhatsApp with no per-message metering, plus an alert to the owner if sending ever stops. Keeps no-shows near Lucia's 9% instead of 15%.
solutions.rationale: Reminders measurably cut no-shows at two restaurants, but several interviewees are fine paying per message and Tomasz won't pay for SMS at all.

solutions.title: Add targeted refundable deposits
solutions.description: Deposit rules by party size and slot (e.g. 6+ guests, Fri/Sat prime time), refundable until 24 hours before and credited to the bill, off by default for small parties and collected online so a card reader isn't needed.
solutions.rationale: Two restaurants run targeted deposits with large measured drops in no-shows, but a café owner and a diner reject deposits outright, so they must stay optional and targeted.

solutions.title: Show live table status and learned turn times
solutions.description: A fast floor view with seated, check-requested and cleared states synced from Square, plus turn times learned per weekday instead of a fixed two hours.
solutions.rationale: Lucia's sticky notes and 25–30 minutes a day are 'does' evidence and hosts ask for the same status, but a one-table café explicitly doesn't want turn times or zones.

solutions.title: Offer freed slots to the waitlist
solutions.description: When a booking cancels or a weeknight slot is empty, text people on the waitlist and let the first to tap take it.
solutions.rationale: Only one owner asked for it ('said'); diner and host evidence about texted waitlists is indirect.

solutions.title: Import history and set up in minutes
solutions.description: Map a BookBistro CSV export automatically and offer a minimal mode with no floor plan, zones or turn times, with migration help scheduled for quiet months like January.
solutions.rationale: Switching barriers are stated by both owners and a floor manager, but nobody has yet tried migrating, so evidence is 'said'.

solutions.title: Price all-in by size of venue
solutions.description: One all-in price including reminders for full-service restaurants (around Lucia's $89–90) and a cheap tier around $15–20 for small cafés with one bookable service.
solutions.rationale: Both owners name concrete prices but they differ by ~5x, so tiers matter more than the exact number; little build effort.

solutions.title: Keep an offline-safe day sheet
solutions.description: Cache the day's book on the device and offer a printable sheet so service continues through Wi-Fi or vendor outages.
solutions.rationale: Only Tomasz raised outages (twice last winter), plus Lucia's broken reminders as a vendor failure; thin evidence.
